For natural-surface trails, the park’s winter freeze/thaw rule permits use only while the ground is frozen, usually early in the morning. This is a trail-protection rule, not confirmation that icy surfaces are safe for a particular visitor.

During winter months, the Freeze/Thaw - Blue Rule applies, which means only use the trails while they are frozen - which is usually in the early morning before the sun thaws the ground or temperatures rise above freezing.

butler-county-regional-transit-authority: BCARE says applicants waiting for processing are offered three consecutive days of rides as a one-time offer available to the public. Confirm the dates and booking arrangements; this does not establish continuing certification.

During the application review process individuals will be offered 3 consecutive days of rides while they are waiting for the application to be processed. This is a one-time ride offer that is available to all of the public.

BCARE’s rider guidelines require all mobility devices to be secured. The page does not describe who performs transfers or the securement procedure; discuss your equipment and assistance needs before travel.
All mobility devices must be secured.

BCARE’s guidelines prohibit eating and drinking onboard and invite reasonable-modification requests. Contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237 to discuss a needed exception before travel; no exception is guaranteed by the page.
Eating or drinking is not permitted on board any vehicles.
Reasonable modifications include changes, exceptions, or adjustments to our rules, policies, practices, and procedures
Reasonable Modification Requests can be made by contacting Customer Service at 513.785.5237
